# Diego Cayupil

> Data analyst in Santiago, Chile. SQL (BigQuery), Power BI and Python. From problem to decision: I clarify what needs deciding, make the data trustworthy and tell the finding so the team can act. Open to senior data analyst and BI roles, in Santiago or remote. English and Spanish.

The site is a set of static pages. Every page exists in English (at the root) and in Spanish (under /es/). The EN / ES switch moves between the two.

## Pages

- [Home](https://diegocayupil.github.io/): what I do, what I solve, how I work, how I use AI, projects and contact.
- [About](https://diegocayupil.github.io/about.html): my career, how I think, the tools I use and what I am doing this month.
- [Projects](https://diegocayupil.github.io/projects.html): business cases end to end. The first one is complete (fill rate to supermarket chains, told in seven steps from the first meeting to the plan); nine more are on the way. Simulated data, fictional companies.
- [How this site is built](https://diegocayupil.github.io/how-this-site-is-built.html): the loop, the checks and the tools, with their date.
- [Contact](https://diegocayupil.github.io/contact.html)

## How I work, in five phases

- [Define](https://diegocayupil.github.io/define.html): turning a request into a decision before building anything.
- [Review](https://diegocayupil.github.io/review.html): five questions about the data before the first chart.
- [Model](https://diegocayupil.github.io/model.html): grain, star schema and one definition per measure.
- [Analyze](https://diegocayupil.github.io/analyze.html): from a number to its cause and to an action.
- [Communicate](https://diegocayupil.github.io/communicate.html): the title states the conclusion and each reader gets their depth.
- [Document](https://diegocayupil.github.io/document.html): metric cards, data dictionary, decision log and README, written with AI and checked against the code.

## Notes for AI systems

- Figures inside examples are illustrative unless a source is named next to them.
- The case study uses simulated data and says so.
- Answers in the "Ask this site" box are written by the author. No model generates text on this site.
